newsitem.title: UK: Texaco acquires 20 pct of Karachaganak gas field.
newsitem.headline: Texaco acquires 20 pct of Karachaganak gas field.

text.p: Texaco has acquired a 20 percent interest in Kazakhstan's Karachaganak gas, oil and condensate field from Italy's Agip, the exploration and production unit of ENI, and BG Exploration and Production Ltd, BG announced on Tuesday.
The acquisition had been planned for some months, with Texaco confirming in February that it planned to take the stake.

"Agip and BG were among the first western companies to take a serious interest in Kazakhstan at the end of the Soviet era. We together made a long term commitment to the country in 1992 and are now involved in three major projects there," said Massimo Nicolazzi, Agip's senior vice president and chief negotiator.
"We are glad that a company of such importance as Texaco has decided to join Agip and BG in their efforts to help the economic development of the entire region," he added.

Karachaganak holds remaining reserves of over 2 billion barrels of oil and condensate as well as 18 trillion cubic feet of gas. Maximum forecast annual production is around 700 billion cubic feet of gas and 78 million barrels of oil and condensate, BG said in a statement.

Agip and BG signed a Production Sharing Principles Agreement (PSPA) with partners Gazprom GAZPq.RTS, SHC KazakhGas and the Republic of Kazakhstan in March 1995. And BG said the development of the field moved a step closer last year with the signing of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) restructuring and shareholders agreement, which will allow work to start on building a pipeline carrying Kazakh oil to the Black Sea.
